The approved snapshot must therefore add the public pricing-status and failure-diagnostic types, replace always-present node outputs with optional node values on failed paths, and record the aligned failure-stage and failure-reason grids on batch and surface artifacts.
change_log.summary: Approve public node-level priceability diagnostics for pricing workflows.

change_log.rationale: The public Python surface now reflects the CLI ownership refactor, the staged runtime exposes the prepared-handle helpers that high-level workflows and tools patch directly, and shared contract helpers are recorded from their defining modules instead of legacy wrapper paths. The approved snapshot must therefore align the guardrails with the thin janiform.cli module, the live staged-runtime helper exports, and the current package-owned contract layout.
change_log.summary: Approve the thin CLI module surface and live staged-runtime helper exports.

change_log.rationale: The high-level fit surface now groups pricing, state-estimation, and fit-inference ownership under dedicated subpackages instead of flat helper modules, and the observed snapshot pricing results are part of the public fit-pricing surface. The approved snapshot must therefore record janiform.calibration.fit.state as the public state-estimation module, keep janiform.pricing.fitted as the canonical pricing ownership package, and align the root calibration exports with the observed snapshot result types that are already part of the supported workflow surface.
change_log.summary: Approve the fit package ownership subpackages and observed snapshot pricing exports.

change_log.rationale: The refactored fit package now uses responsibility-based internal names instead of leaking the old high_level label through private implementation symbols, so the approved snapshot records the cleaned model persistence constant name without changing the serialized schema value.
change_log.summary: Record the fit package naming cleanup in the approved Python API snapshot.

change_log.rationale: The high-level fit API now separates the simple raising path from the reporting path, so JaniformEstimator.fit no longer changes shape based on a boolean flag and the public surface records JaniformFitResult plus the explicit fit_with_report entrypoint.
change_log.summary: Approve the split high-level fit and fit_with_report API surface.

change_log.rationale: The fit package now treats execution, inference, preparation, and runtime helpers as internal _-prefixed implementation modules, removes estimator compatibility base classes from the public contract metadata, and keeps janiform.calibration.fit.state focused on public state-estimation contracts rather than implementation helpers.
change_log.summary: Curate the fit package boundary around public facades and internal workflow modules.

change_log.rationale: The calibration root now exposes only the main high-level fit facade and root-level validation errors. Internal fitted-model helper behavior now lives in private _runtime service modules instead of on JaniformModel.
change_log.summary: Shrink the calibration root and remove model-private runtime helper exports.

change_log.rationale: The fitted-model pricing package now exposes grids, surface, summaries, and market_snapshot as explicit public concept modules. Internal pricing helpers live under internal and market_snapshot subpackages instead of underscore helper files.
change_log.summary: Reshape fitted-model pricing around concept modules and subpackages.

change_log.rationale: The janiform.calibration.fit root now stays focused on the main estimator, fitted model, and fit-result classes, while pricing and state contracts are imported from their ownership submodules.
change_log.summary: Narrow janiform.calibration.fit to the curated high-level surface.

change_log.rationale: The option-grid pricing surface now uses grid-based contract names that match JaniformModel.price_option_grids, so callers no longer have to translate between grouped-batch naming and the public method vocabulary.
change_log.summary: Rename grouped-batch option pricing contracts to grid-based names.

change_log.rationale: Give market_snapshot tabular inputs a real public owner module and import public pricing types in JaniformModel from their owning modules instead of the pricing barrel or private workflow modules.
change_log.summary: Add market_snapshot.inputs as the public owner of TabularFrameInput and align model imports with owner modules.

change_log.rationale: The shared janiform.contracts package now reexports every public require_* helper that lives in janiform.contracts.base, while package-internal modules import those helpers from the defining base module instead of the public barrel. The approved snapshot must therefore widen the janiform.contracts public surface to include the remaining validation helpers without preserving barrel imports inside the package.
change_log.summary: Approve the full shared require_* helper surface on janiform.contracts.

change_log.rationale: The market-data calibration request now exposes explicit joint-refinement option refinement controls for candidate shortlist sizing and audit-tier pricing, while keeping both controls optional and defaulted for normal calibration.
change_log.summary: Expose joint-refinement option refinement and audit controls on the market-data request.

change_log.rationale: The high-level JaniformEstimator and market-data request now expose a dynamics-search restart count so users can adjust restart frontier breadth without constructing staged execution inputs.
change_log.summary: Expose dynamics-search restart count on high-level calibration.

change_log.rationale: The high-level calibration API now exposes resume settings and pricing-interval schedule policy on JaniformEstimator, simulation results use the shared SimulationKind discriminator, and fitted-model pricing adds public observed option-surface result types under janiform.pricing.fitted and janiform.pricing.fitted.market_surface.
change_log.summary: Approve the resume-aware high-level calibration surface and public observed option-surface pricing results.

change_log.rationale: The checked-in public API snapshot is already current, and the guardrail approval hash must match that exact snapshot serialization so the approval manifest validates the repository state.
change_log.summary: Align the public API approval manifest with the checked-in snapshot hash.

change_log.rationale: The sufficient-statistics contracts are now owned by janiform.sufficient_statistics instead of janiform.risk, with the old public type names replaced directly because the package is pre-v0.1 and does not carry compatibility aliases.
change_log.summary: Approve the sufficient-statistics package rename.

change_log.rationale: Preset registry lookup now resolves through the Rust native registry for bundled and user-registered presets, so the Python public surface no longer exposes separate BuiltInPresetRegistry and UserPresetRegistry owner classes.
change_log.summary: Approve the Rust-owned preset registry surface.

change_log.rationale: Preset artifact contracts and native artifact serialization helpers now live under janiform.calibration.presets.artifacts, while janiform.calibration.presets.registry only exposes registry/index/export contracts.
change_log.summary: Approve the split preset artifact and registry ownership surfaces.

change_log.rationale: Market-data preparation now accepts the native worker-count override at the Python boundary so high-level fitting and direct market-data preparation use the same Rust preparation path.
change_log.summary: Approve the Rust-backed market-data preparation boundary.

change_log.rationale: High-level fit reports and fitted-model payloads no longer retain full stage payloads or candidate datasets across the Rust-to-Python boundary. Python receives compact staged summaries and model metadata while Rust owns persisted stage artifacts and fitted parameter selection. The fitted-model module no longer exposes the imported model-persistence schema constant through a fake-private alias.
change_log.summary: Remove retained stage payloads from the high-level fit report surface.

change_log.rationale: High-level fit now exposes the same typed progress callback boundary as simulation from a model artifact, so users can observe Rust-owned workflow progress without Python owning a second progress implementation.
change_log.summary: Approve typed fit progress callback events.

change_log.rationale: Simulation entrypoints now accept terminal progress mode at the Python boundary so Rust owns simulation progress UX while Python remains a thin native adapter. The existing progress callback remains an event observation hook rather than the CLI UX path.
change_log.summary: Approve Rust-owned simulation terminal progress boundaries.

change_log.rationale: Pricing surface workflows now expose the same typed progress callback boundary as fit and simulation, so users can observe Rust-owned workflow progress without Python owning a separate progress implementation.
change_log.summary: Approve typed pricing progress callback events.

change_log.rationale: Preset artifact handling now exposes the public PresetArtifact union for generic artifact passing while PresetRegistry exposes typed category-specific resolver methods. The dynamic resolver is private so user code can avoid casts when requesting a known preset category.
change_log.summary: Approve typed preset registry resolution methods.

change_log.rationale: Preset dependency collection now uses snapshot naming in the Python API so callers do not mistake the method for a side-effecting file export. The CLI export command still writes the resolved snapshot payload to stdout.
change_log.summary: Rename resolved preset export API to resolved preset snapshot API.

change_log.rationale: The Python CLI implementation and its public janiform.cli constants module have been retired. The wheel entrypoint now delegates directly into the Rust CLI through the native boundary, so the public Python API snapshot no longer advertises Python-owned CLI constants or exit-code contracts.
change_log.summary: Remove the retired Python CLI public surface.

change_log.rationale: Python no longer owns CLI-oriented stylized-fact markdown rendering. Rust validation and CLI rendering own that output path, while Python keeps the typed report contracts and Plotly figure adapter for library workflows.
change_log.summary: Remove the Python stylized-fact markdown renderer.

change_log.rationale: Rust owns workflow progress event schemas and serializes callback payloads across the Python boundary, so Python no longer exposes duplicate event contracts or phase enums.
change_log.summary: Remove Python-owned workflow progress event contracts from the public API.

change_log.rationale: The fitted model is now owned by janiform.model, simulation result inspection is owned by janiform.simulation, and fitted-model option pricing contracts live under janiform.pricing.fitted. The calibration fit package now keeps only the estimator, fit report, and fit result surface.
change_log.summary: Move model, simulation result, and fitted-pricing API ownership out of calibration fit.

change_log.rationale: Prepared calibration execution artifact persistence is no longer a Python-owned workflow output. Rust owns persisted workflow artifacts, so the public market-data output preferences contract no longer exposes the staged execution input emission switch.
change_log.summary: Remove the Python prepared-execution artifact emission preference.

change_log.rationale: Janiform does not need native plot support for stylized facts initially. Let people choose what to plot and build their plots of this themselves if they need them.
change_log.summary: Remove native plot support for stylized facts from Janiform initial release.

change_log.rationale: Market-data source summaries now expose invalid source-row drops separately from duplicate drops so option-surface quote filtering is visible to Python callers and generated reports.
change_log.summary: Expose invalid-row counts in market-data source summaries.

change_log.rationale: Observed-options pricing now returns native result payloads without embedding the large raw grid-batch result inside each snapshot. The Python ergonomic snapshot wrapper therefore treats raw_result as optional while preserving the priced node contract.
change_log.summary: Make observed snapshot raw grid payload optional.

change_log.rationale: Calibration accepts an optional user-provided tick size, seeded simulation exposes fitted return-mark and tick-grid observation inputs, and coarse interval simulation carries the same fitted observation contracts as seeded tick simulation instead of using a different interval policy.
change_log.summary: Expose fitted tick-grid and return-mark runtime inputs.

change_log.rationale: Calibration now exposes option refinement and finalization as first-class staged calibration steps, records deterministic calibration effort and warning policy controls, and carries fitted return-mark factors through public vanilla-option pricing request contracts so pricing and staged calibration use the same validated runtime inputs.
change_log.summary: Approve staged option refinement, finalization, and pricing runtime contract fields.

change_log.rationale: Observed-options pricing now exposes an optional physical terminal-distribution diagnostic request and result so Python callers can compare model-P volatility equivalents with observed and model-Q option surfaces without owning artifact persistence.
change_log.summary: Expose observed-options physical distribution diagnostics.

change_log.rationale: Return-size seasonality has been removed from the public runtime contracts. Simulation and pricing now carry explicit Hawkes-excitation return-clock exposure parameters so deterministic calendar seasonality remains an event-intensity input rather than a direct return-size scaler.
change_log.summary: Replace public return-mark runtime fields with return-clock exposure parameters.

change_log.rationale: Long variance is now a first-class public runtime state and parameter contract across calibration, simulation, and pricing, and terminal-affine option pricing reports terminal-affine diagnostics instead of the prior transform-stage diagnostic fields.
change_log.summary: Approve public long-variance runtime contracts and terminal-affine pricing diagnostics.

change_log.rationale: News and gap shocks now use shape-only unit-mean Gamma severity and coupled Gamma-normal return marks with open and closed surprise intensity controls, so the public contracts remove the legacy free Gamma scale, Kou mark, coupled-gap, and single surprise-intensity fields.
change_log.summary: Approve public coupled Gamma-normal news shock contracts.

change_log.rationale: Option workflows now expose price-coordinate policy, resolved coordinate diagnostics, warning summaries, and opt-in calibration diagnostics through the public Python fit and market-data surfaces.
change_log.summary: Approve public price-coordinate and calibration diagnostic controls.

change_log.rationale: Calibration requests now accept optional coarse historical data and an explicit tick-objective usage policy, so the public contract snapshot must include the new typed request fields and diagnostics.
change_log.summary: Expose multi-resolution coarse data evidence in the Python calibration boundary.

change_log.rationale: Coarse historical bars now expose typed timestamp semantics so the default industry-standard open-time interpretation is explicit while close-time sources remain selectable.
change_log.summary: Expose coarse timestamp semantics in the Python calibration boundary.

change_log.rationale: The public calibration boundary now names optional lower-frequency OHLCV and close-only inputs as coarse data, matching the existing tick data wording and avoiding a finance-ambiguous training label.
change_log.summary: Rename lower-frequency calibration evidence fields and CLI flags to coarse data.
